verdict.rationale: OpenTofu is an open-source, Linux Foundation-governed tool that users install and run on their own infrastructure. The docs cover many install paths: Homebrew, standalone binaries for Linux/macOS/Windows/FreeBSD, and an official OCI container image on GHCR. The source and nightly builds are public on GitHub, state can be stored locally with at-rest encryption, and community reports of client migrations confirm teams run it themselves. missing for 10: the specific license is not named in the evidence (a community user notes it is not clearly shown on the website), and there is no explicit air-gapped or self-hosted registry guidance.
